title: adaptive on-call tempo controller and playbook sample harness
author: Maya Liu
description: Motivation: Pager thrash and noisy handoffs are a recurring source of toil. This PR implements an adaptive "tempo controller" that smooths incident routing and an ephemeral playbook hooks surface to let runbooks execute short-lived diagnostics in a sandboxed environment. The controller applies a time-decay weighting to recent alert activity, uses configurable cooldown windows per service/route, and exposes a small policy DSL for schedule-aware routing (e.g. prefer on-call A during business hours, fallback to rotation B with exponential backoff at night). The playbook sample harness enables CI validation for playbook snippets and short-lived diagnostic scripts: it spins up ephemeral containers, verifies required telemetry access, and validates that remediation steps are idempotent and time-bounded. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of tempo controller core scheduler and policy engine - [x] Ephemeral playbook hook API and sandbox runner - [x] Unit tests for scheduling heuristics and playbook harness - [x] Integration tests simulating alert bursts and handoffs - [x] Docs (ops runbook + examples) - [x] Benchmarks showing reduced handoff churn in synthetic workload Summary of risk: this changes on-call routing logic; default policies are conservative and off by default. We ship the controller disabled on main; ops can opt-in per-service via config. Related: builds on prior incident-bot alert normalization work (ENG-3320) and complements the runbook serialiser in incident-bot (ENG-4102).

review_thread: Diego Ramos: Nice direction — can we add an explicit test for sequential bursts that cross the cooldown boundary? I saw one flake in CI that looks related.
Maya Liu: Added a targeted test (test_tempo_controller::test_burst_crossing_cooldown) and fixed a cancellation race that could leave a timer firing after a handler was removed.
Samir Khan: Sandbox runner looks good, but we need to ensure secrets are never mounted into ephemeral containers. Please document the secret access pattern.
Maya Liu: Updated docs to clarify the minimal telemetry role required and added a hard check that prevents accidental host-mounted /etc/credentials into the sandbox.
Ava Patel: Verified bench runs; the synthetic scenario reduces visible handoffs across rotations by ~8%. Approving after addressing Samir's docs note.
Diego Ramos: Approving — small nit on a doc wording changed in a followup commit.

release_notes:
- Introduces an opt-in "tempo controller" to smooth on-call routing and reduce handoff churn.
- Adds ephemeral playbook hooks and a CI harness to validate short-lived diagnostic runbooks.
- Default OFF on main; operators must opt-in per-service.
- Includes unit/integration tests and docs with example policies.
notes: Operational impact: enable behind feature flag: slo.tempo_controller.enabled. Recommend gradual rollout: enable for non-critical services first and monitor handoff-count metric (slo.oncall.handoffs_per_hour).
